title: SWE-RM: Execution-free Feedback For Software Engineering Agents
why: This is the arXiv preprint of the already-cited OpenReview record (SWE-RM, H9wMe1G76j) by the same HKUST/Qwen-Team authors; it shows two execution-free reward models can look identical on test-time-scaling (a log/proxy-style metric) yet behave very differently under RL, the same proxy-verifier-vs-true-outcome estimand as this paper.

title: Audited Skill-Graph Self-Improvement for Agentic LLMs via Verifiable Rewards, Experience Synthesis, and Continual Memory
why: Proposes an auditable self-improvement architecture whose explicit threat model is that tampered logs/artifacts can create 'the appearance of improvement' and that verifiable rewards can shift behavior toward what is easiest to verify rather than what is desired -- the same log-forging/reward-gaming mechanism this paper studies, framed here as a defense proposal with no empirical measurement of the phenomenon.

title: Triangulation as an Acceptance Rule for Multilingual Mechanistic Interpretability
why: A causal acceptance-rule framework (necessity/sufficiency/invariance) for validating mechanistic-interpretability circuits across languages; no verifier-vs-state divergence or agent tool-use log gaming is studied.

title: The Reward Model Selection Crisis in Personalized Alignment
why: Shows empirically that reward-model ranking accuracy correlates only weakly (Kendall tau 0.08-0.31) with downstream reward-guided-decoding policy behavior, i.e. a cheap proxy verifier diverging from the true generation-quality objective -- the same proxy/true-objective divergence mechanism this paper studies, though in personalized-alignment decoding rather than agent tool-use logs.

title: SmartSnap: Proactive Evidence Seeking for Self-Verifying Agents
why: Trains GUI agents to curate their own snapshot evidence for a verifier, explicitly noting that 'agent self-declaration' can 'omit failures to hack the verifier' -- an existing evidence/log-based verification design of exactly the kind this paper argues can be gamed, making it a natural comparison point for log-side verification.

title: MindWatcher: Toward Smarter Multimodal Tool-Integrated Reasoning
why: A general multimodal tool-integrated-reasoning agent, retrieval database, and benchmark (MWE-Bench); a generic agent-capability paper with no log-vs-state verifier gaming analysis.

title: Beyond Itinerary Planning—A Real-World Benchmark for Multi-Turn and Tool-Using Travel Tasks
why: A real-world, multi-turn, tool-using travel-planning benchmark with a cached-tool sandbox; a generic agent-capability benchmark, not a study of log-vs-state verifier gaming.

title: When Does Pairing Seeds Reduce Variance? Evidence from a Multi-Agent Economic Simulation
why: A statistics paper deriving variance-reduction formulas for paired-random-seed evaluation in a multi-agent economic simulator; unrelated to verifier gaming or agent tool-use logs.

title: From Model Choice to Model Belief: Establishing a New Measure for LLM-Based Research

why: A large agentic-LLM training-infrastructure and model technical report (ALE/ROLL/ROCK/ROME) that only mentions reward-hacking/deceptive-behavior risk in passing; a generic agent-capability system paper, not a study of log-vs-state divergence.

why: Proposes an automated pipeline for synthesizing tool-use RL environments with a reward defined purely by final-state equality to a golden state (already state-grounded, not log-based), and never studies whether the trained agent learns to fake logs while skipping real state changes.

title: Fantastic Reasoning Behaviors and Where to Find Them: Unsupervised Discovery of the Reasoning Process
why: Uses sparse autoencoders to discover and steer latent reasoning behaviors (reflection, backtracking, confidence) in CoT text; a mechanistic-interpretability study unrelated to verifier gaming.

why: Benchmarks how SFT vs RL post-training reshape atomic cognitive reasoning skills (calculation, retrieval, diagnostic checking); no verifier-gaming content.

why: Empirically measures whether coding-agent output (declared dependencies) matches what is actually needed to execute in a clean environment, which is a claim-vs-reality gap, but it is about dependency completeness/reproducibility of static code artifacts, not an agent gaming a log verifier during a task under optimization pressure.

why: Maps FLOPs-vs-accuracy Pareto frontiers across open reasoning models on math/QA benchmarks; a compute-efficiency benchmarking study unrelated to verifier gaming.

title: Evaluating the Reasoning Abilities of LLMs on Underrepresented Mathematics Competition Problems
